summary.en: The kata examination every BJA dan grade promotion requires alongside the skills assessment, and the one part of a promotion that is examined on its own terms: one named kata for each grade, certified at Level 1 on the competitive pathway and Level 2 on the technical one. It need not be taken on the same day as the skills assessment, or in the same year.

note.en: Transcribed from the BJA kata requirements for promotions from 1 January 2026, with the rules on who may examine and when from the scheme's published questions and answers. The forms are the authority; where this page and a current BJA form disagree, the form wins.

marking.en: The pass marks are percentages: 60 per cent for Level 1 and 65 per cent for Level 2. Level 1 is an entry level pass, and a candidate who has prepared properly, including a relevant BJA kata course, should reach it. Level 2 may be taken six months after a Level 1 pass; going straight to Level 2 is exceptional and needs the evaluation of a Senior Kata Examiner or higher. A BJA Senior Examiner, Kata Examiner or Senior Kata Examiner may examine kata. Attending a course does not exempt anyone: an attendance certificate is not a pass, and from 1 January 2026 attendance certificates are no longer issued.

requirement.en: The kata named for the grade being taken. Required on the competitive pathway.
The correct techniques, in the correct order, with technical competence and the protocol that surrounds the kata.
The kata named for the grade being taken. Required on the technical pathway.
Everything Level 1 asks for, performed with the skill, timing and partnership a higher grade is expected to show.

notes.en: One kata per grade, and only the one for the grade being taken: a candidate going for 4th Dan does not repeat the kata of the three grades below. The competitive pathway needs a Level 1 certificate in it, the technical pathway a Level 2.

items.text: For 6th Dan, in addition to the five kata above, a minimum BJA Level 1 certificate in Koshiki-no-kata

notes.en: A 60 per cent pass, and very much an entry level one.
A 65 per cent pass, taken no sooner than six months after Level 1. The same kata again, with everything sharper.
